correctness.rationale: The defining ideal relations constrain {x,y}=f precisely to (x^a y^b); Jacobi is automatic for alternating biderivations of a two-generator commutative algebra even in characteristic two. For f=f0*g the central kernel contains that of f0 and equals it for unit g. The monomial derivative criterion produces four disjoint exponent classes and the dimension formula. A nonzero f gives two independent Hamiltonian-coordinate images, bounding centre codimension below by 2, and socle f attains it. Invertibility criterion follows from the local algebra maximal ideal. Direct finite-field Gaussian-elimination and Jacobi checks in verify.py confirm sampled and exhaustive cases, including F4; tests are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The Poisson centre (degree-zero Poisson cohomology) is an invariant explicitly studied in the motivating Launois–Richard paper. The theorem identifies the full parameter space of Poisson brackets on a natural two-parameter family of Artin complete intersections, proves the sharp generic and maximal centre dimensions, and exhibits modular congruence jumps (for m=n=3: 2 over characteristic zero, 6 in characteristic two, 1 in characteristic three). It quantifies the generic fraction over every finite field and characterizes when unit-valued brackets occur. The uniform congruence structure and exact extremal statement are not isolated exercises or arbitrary slices.
